newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast prods flat amid neutral supply data.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast prods flat amid neutral supply data.

text.p: Wholesale prices for U.S. West Coast refined petroleum products were flat Tuesday, as higher energy futures prices and year-on-year shorftall kept gasoline firm despite an inventory build last week.

West Coast (PADD IV) gasoline stocks rose 323,000 barrels for the week ended April 4, but stood 2.3 million barrels below the same period last year, according to American Petroleum Institute (API), an industry trade group.
"We're still at extremely low inventories," one trader said. Prices, which fell sharply last weeek "lost their downward momentum," Monday and Tuesday, he said.
Futures markets, which influence spot prices, rose slightly Tuesday, with gasoline for May delivery up 0.45 cents a gallon as demand for immediate barrels rose.
Crude futures also rose, up 12 cents to $19.35 a barrel.
CARB gasoline in San Francisco sold for 70 cents a gallon Tuesday, in line with Monday's levels.
CARB gasoline in Los Angeles remained 71/73 cents a gallon Tuesday, traders said, as trade turned quiet late.
Distillates were also quiet, staying at Monday's levels.
